trap_patterns.description: Students may choose chemically implausible or incomplete products when predicting reactions.
examples: Predicting products requires recognizing reaction pattern before writing products.

trap_patterns.description: Students may identify the correct reaction but lose marks on balancing or coefficient precision.
examples: Correct reaction identification but incorrect balancing.

trap_patterns.description: Students may confuse reaction categories even when the reaction itself is recognized correctly.
examples: Confusing synthesis, decomposition, combustion, and displacement types.

trap_patterns.description: Chemical state symbols and notation accuracy appear to matter and may act as a precision trap.
Some questions appear to require transfer from learned reaction patterns into applied or real-world contexts.
examples: Application questions may require concept transfer rather than direct recall.

trap_patterns.description: Written-response expectations may penalize incomplete reasoning, not just factual errors.
examples: Use full sentences or explain reasoning clearly.

trap_patterns.description: The assessment appears to shift across sections, which can change how students must respond and manage time.
